description: A four-panel set of bright-field transmission electron micrographs (TEM) tracking dislocation-substructure evolution in the austenite of 1.2C steel during tensile deformation. All panels are greyscale TEM images with a white rectangular scale bar in the lower-right corner; the bars read 1 µm in (a) and (b) and 0.5 µm in (c) and (d), so the lower two panels are at higher magnification. (a), labelled "a", shows a few widely spaced, straight, sub-parallel slip traces crossing a relatively featureless matrix, with darker tangled patches at the top-left and right edges. (b), labelled "b", shows several sets of intersecting parallel bands producing a rectangular, grid-like Taylor-lattice-type arrangement. (c), labelled "c", shows dense, closely spaced elongated bright and dark microbands running diagonally across the field with mottled contrast between them. (d), labelled "d", shows microbands in more than one direction crossing and blocking each other in a blocky pattern. No crystallographic indices, diffraction patterns, axis labels or numeric strain values are printed on the pixels; the strain values (ε 0.02, 0.07, 0.3, 0.4) come only from the caption and citing text. The four panels together demonstrate the sequential substructure sequence planar slip → Taylor lattice → microbands → microband interaction with increasing tensile strain in 1.2C steel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar. Sparsely distributed straight, sub-parallel slip traces crossing a smooth matrix; darker tangled dislocation patches at the top-left and right edges. Labelled 'a'.

Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar. Several intersecting sets of parallel bands forming a rectangular, blocky grid pattern consistent with a Taylor lattice; darker heavily dislocated regions on the left. Labelled 'b'.

Bright-field TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar (higher magnification). Dense, closely spaced bright and dark elongated bands (microbands) aligned diagonally, with mottled dark contrast between the bands. Labelled 'c'.

Bright-field TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar (higher magnification). Multiply oriented, closely spaced microbands crossing and intersecting each other, forming a blocky, heavily contrasted structure. Labelled 'd'.

observations.observation: The group consists of four bright-field TEM micrographs labelled a, b, c and d, each carrying a white scale bar in the lower-right corner.
The scale bars read 1 µm in panels (a) and (b) and 0.5 µm in panels (c) and (d), so panels (c) and (d) are imaged at higher magnification.
Panel (a) shows only a few widely spaced, straight, sub-parallel slip traces crossing a comparatively featureless matrix.
Panel (b) shows several intersecting sets of parallel bands producing a rectangular grid-like (Taylor lattice) arrangement, with darker heavily dislocated regions on the left side.
Panel (c) shows dense, closely spaced, elongated bright and dark bands oriented diagonally, i.e. well developed microbands, with mottled contrast between them.
Panel (d) shows microbands in more than one direction crossing and intersecting one another in a blocky pattern.
No crystallographic indices, diffraction patterns, axis labels or printed strain values appear on any panel; the only printed text is the panel letters a-d and the scale-bar labels 1 µm / 0.5 µm.
The caption states panel (a) is planar slip at ε 0.02 in 1.2C steel.
The caption states panel (b) is a Taylor lattice at ε 0.07, panel (c) well developed microbands at ε 0.3, and panel (d) interaction of the microbands at ε 0.4.

The citing text states that in 1.2C steel the planar slip develops in the primary deformation stage (Fig. 8(a)), followed by Taylor lattice (Fig. 8(b)) and microbands (Fig. 8(c)) in the intermediate stage, and microband interaction in the final stage (Fig. 8(d)).

The citing text attributes the multi-stage strain-hardening behaviour of the fully austenitic 1.2C steel to this variation of dislocation structures, the third stage (microband interaction) being absent in 0.5C and 0.8C steels.

The citing text asserts that microband interaction was not observed under TEM in 0.5C and 0.8C steels because of their limited plastic deformation capability, which is linked to their lower tensile ductility; this figure itself shows only 1.2C steel.

measured_quantities: magnification (panel-to-panel, via 1 µm vs 0.5 µm scale bars)
unreadable_items: panels (c) and (d): grainy, low-contrast rendering means individual microband boundaries and the exact number of microband families cannot be reliably counted
no diffraction patterns or Miller indices are present in any panel, so the crystallography of the slip traces/microbands cannot be read from this figure
the strain values ε 0.02, 0.07, 0.3 and 0.4 are not printed on the images and are taken from the caption/citing text only
